page: Microsoft Azure HX176-96rs is a high-performance computing virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel processor. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs. It is architected for demanding compute workloads requiring high memory capacity and inter-node networking, supporting RDMA capability alongside Azure Premium Storage integrations.

Memory capacity on the HX176-96rs is 1408.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-core allocation of 14.67 GB per vCPU. The server bundles 4355 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, delivering fast local scratch space and high I/O throughput. There are zero hardware accelerators or GPUs configured on this type, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided by default.

The high ratio of memory per core and substantial bundled local NVMe storage position the HX176-96rs for data-heavy computing environments without the overhead of physical GPU infrastructure. The availability of RDMA networking coupled with dedicated vCPUs suits tightly coupled distributed simulations, electronic design automation, finite element analysis, in-memory databases, and large-scale technical computing workloads.
